en: The Ritual for the Rain-Prayer Altar from the Mahāmegha Sūtra:
When there is a severe drought and one wishes to pray for rain, construct an altar in an open space.
Clear away all shards, rubble, and impure objects; hang up a blue canopy and blue banners, and prepare fragrant mud.
Having smeared and swept the ground, construct a square altar.
In the center of the altar, paint a pond of the seven treasures;
within the pond, paint the palace of the Sāgara Dragon King.
Within the dragon palace, there is the scene of the Tathāgata Śākyamuni preaching the Dharma.
To the right of the Buddha, draw the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara;
to the left of the Buddha, draw the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi and others as his attendants.
To the right of the Buddha, paint the Dragon King Cakravartī, Lord of the Trichiliocosm;
to the left of the Buddha, paint the two Dragon Kings Nanda and Upananda.
On the four sides of the maṇḍala,
use cow dung juice to draw a nāga king on each side;
on the eastern side, draw one nāga king.
He has one body with three heads,
measuring three cubits in length,
and is surrounded by his retinue.
Furthermore, in the southern direction, one should paint a nāga king with five heads on a single body,
measuring five cubits in length.
Together with their retinues,
one should also paint a nāga king in the western direction,
having seven heads on a single body.
It should be seven cubits in length and surrounded by its retinue.
Furthermore, in the northern direction, one should paint a nāga king.
He has one body with nine heads,
measuring nine cubits in length,
and is surrounded by his retinue.
They all dwell within dark blue-black clouds;
from the midpoint of their bodies downward, they have the form of snakes,
with their tails submerged in the pools.
From the upper half of their bodies upward, they take the form of bodhisattvas;
all emerge from the pond with palms joined at the four corners of the maṇḍala.
Place four vases filled with clear water.
According to one's means,
all food, drink, fruits, and so forth should be dyed blue.
With a sincere and pure mind, arrange the offerings;
burn incense and scatter blue flowers.
All items used within the *maṇḍala* should be made blue.
If the person praying for rain is an ordained bhikṣu,
he should be fully endowed with the Vinaya discipline;
if he is a layperson, he should receive the eight precepts.
When performing the ritual,
one should consume the "three white foods" and bathe daily in fragrant water.
Wearing new, clean blue robes,
one should sit upon a seat made of blue materials on the western side of the altar.
Then, having applied fragrance to the hands,
one should first empower oneself through the three secrets and protect the maṇḍala site.
Place this Mahāmegha Sūtra upon the table.
Generate great compassion for all sentient beings and,
with utmost sincerity, invoke the empowerment of all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas.
With sincere devotion day and night,
read this Mahāmegha Sūtra;
alternatively, two, three, or even up to seven people may take turns reading and reciting it.
The sound of the sutra should not be interrupted.
During times of severe drought,
one should recite this Mahāmegha Sūtra according to the ritual instructions in this manner.
After one day, two days, or even up to seven days,
a steady downpour of sweet rain will surely fall;
yet if the calamity is grave and it does not rain, [the ritual must be performed again].
If it still does not rain, one must certainly invoke a descent of sweet rain.
Even if the great ocean should exceed its bounds or overflow its tides,
by performing the ritual methods and reciting this sutra according to the instructions, [the calamity will cease].
There is no reason for it not to be effective.
One should make a vow and dedicate the merit arising from reciting the sutra to all the nāgas,
wishing that they may all be freed from their various sufferings and hardships.
The Ritual for the Rain-Prayer Altar from the Mahāmegha Sūtra: Generating the Unsurpassed Bodhicitta to Send Down Sweet Rain for All Sentient Beings.
